title: ALMA-LEGUS. I. The Influence of Galaxy Morphology on Molecular Cloud Properties
question: Which molecular cloud properties differ between barred spiral NGC 1313 and flocculent spiral NGC 7793 (similar mass, metallicity and SFR) and could explain NGC 1313 forming many more massive young star clusters

data.angular_resolution: matched to 13 pc in both galaxies (after smoothing to a circular beam)
data.sensitivity: ~0.2 K surface brightness sensitivity, matched between galaxies

what.value: LEGUS star cluster catalogs (masses, ages, extinctions) for NGC 1313 and NGC 7793

evidence.quote: we use catalogs of star clusters and their SED-fitted properties from the LEGUS collaboration, which used the methodology described in (cite: Adamo17)

what.value: Galaxy SFR (GALEX far-UV based), stellar mass and HI mass used in Table 1

evidence.quote: Calculated by (cite: Calzetti15) using GALEX far-UV images, dust corrected with methods of (cite: Lee09)

what.value: NGC 1313 oxygen abundance 8.4+-0.1, no radial gradient

evidence.quote: For NGC 1313, we use an oxygen abundance of $12+\log{\text{(O/H)}}=8.4\pm0.1$ with no radial gradient in the galaxy (cite: WalshRoy97).

what.value: NGC 7793 radial oxygen abundance gradient (8.572 - 0.054 dex/kpc x R_gal)

evidence.quote: NGC 7793 has a measured radial gradient of $12+\log{\text{(O/H)}}=8.572 - 0.054$ dex kpc$^{-1} \times R_\text{gal}$ (cite: Stanghellini15).
Using a solar oxygen abundance of $12+\log{\text{(O/H)}}=8.69$ (cite: Asplund09)

what.value: Alternative NGC 7793 metallicity gradient (8.945 - 0.083 dex/kpc x R_gal), tested but not adopted

evidence.quote: which instead finds $12+\log{\text{(O/H)}}=8.945 - 0.083$ dex kpc$^{-1} \times R_\text{gal}$

what.value: Line used to flag clusters with age-reddening degeneracy (E(B-V) versus log(Age))

evidence.quote: we remove the clusters that fall above the E(B-V)-log(Age) line from (cite: Whitmore23) only when comparing age measurements between the two galaxies
the standard 10% ALMA flux calibration uncertainty (cite: Fomalont14)

what.value: Milky Way size-linewidth reference a0 = 1.0+-0.1, a1 = 0.5+-0.05

evidence.quote: which found $a_0 = 1.0\pm0.1$ and $a_1 = 0.5\pm0.05$ for clouds mapped in CO(1-0) in the disk of the Milky Way

recipe.goal: calibrate, image and smooth the CO(2-1) cubes
recipe.method: ALMA pipeline calibration, CASA imaging with Briggs weighting, then smoothing both cubes to a common circular 13 pc beam

Use LEGUS catalogs (Cardelli89 extinction law, averaged aperture correction, Padova tracks via Yggdrasil), keep all cluster candidates, merge east and west maps using the better-fit entry for duplicates, drop age-degenerate clusters only for age comparisons
key_parameters: massive clusters M > 1e4 Msun; young clusters age < 10 Myr
67 overlapping clusters in NGC 1313, 47 in NGC 7793
assumptions: SFR fraction inside the LEGUS footprint from GALEX far-UV light used to scale cluster counts to the full galaxy

recipe.goal: decompose the CO cube into dendrogram structures and clumps
recipe.method: astrodendro hierarchical dendrograms (used for size-linewidth and virial analysis) and quickclump non-overlapping clumps (used for property distributions and counts)
key_parameters: astrodendro: min_value=3 sigma, min_delta=2.5 sigma, min_npix=2 beams
quickclump: Tcutoff=4 sigma, dTleaf=4 sigma, Npixmin=2 beams (65 voxels for NGC 1313, 70 for NGC 7793)
assumptions: Dendrograms count emission multiple times so are used only where multiple counting is allowed

recipe.goal: compute cloud masses with a metallicity-dependent X_CO
recipe.method: X_CO(2-1) from Gong20 (function of T_peak, beam size 13 pc, metallicity), H2 column density summed over pixel area, times 1.4 for total gas mass
key_parameters: Z = 0.51 Zsun (NGC 1313); Z = (0.56-0.76) Zsun (NGC 7793, Stanghellini15 gradient)
mass error = 10% flux calibration added in quadrature with rms noise error
assumptions: factor 1.4 (mean mass per hydrogen atom, all hydrogen molecular)
NGC 1313 metallicity with no radial gradient; solar 12+log(O/H) = 8.69

recipe.goal: measure velocity dispersion and radius of each structure
recipe.method: Gaussian fit to the intensity-weighted mean line profile, deconvolved with channel width; ellipse fit to half-power contours, converted to effective radius and deconvolved with the beam, geometric mean of axes
key_parameters: channel width 1.33 km/s with FWHM = 2.35 sigma; beam radius 6.5 pc; effective radius factor 1.91
structures with deconvolved sigma_v < 0.1 x velocity resolution or R < 0.1 x beam size removed

recipe.goal: derive surface density, virial parameter, external pressure and free-fall time
recipe.method: Sigma = M / area; alpha_vir = 5 sigma_v^2 R / (G M); P_e = 3 Pi M sigma_v^2 / (4 pi R^3); t_ff = sqrt(pi^2 R^3 / (8 G M))
key_parameters: Pi = 0.5 for external pressure; collapse threshold alpha_vir < 1, unbound above 2
assumptions: cloud in pressure equilibrium with surrounding medium for P_e

recipe.method: Power-law sigma_v = a0 R^a1 fit to dendrogram structures with orthogonal distance regression, slope fixed at a1 = 0.5, intercept fitted per galaxy
key_parameters: 2-D Gaussian KDE (scipy.stats, Scott's rule bandwidth) used only to display the point distribution
assumptions: fixed slope 0.5, chosen because fitted slopes in the literature vary widely with resolution, tracer and method

recipe.goal: assess virial state of dendrogram structures
recipe.method: Plot sigma_v^2/R against surface density for each dendrogram structure with the alpha_vir = 1 line and compare scatter between galaxies
assumptions: only gravitational and kinetic energies considered; external pressure and magnetic fields neglected in the plot

recipe.goal: compare cloud and cluster property distributions between galaxies
recipe.method: Histograms, KDEs and CDFs of non-overlapping clumps; two-sample KS and AD tests on 1000 random subsamples, averaging p-values
assumptions: full-sample KS/AD tests are overpowered at large N, so subsampling is used only to rank which properties differ most

recipe.goal: test spatial correlation of bound clouds and cloud properties with young clusters
recipe.method: Build gridded density maps of clouds, bound clouds and young clusters and compute correlation coefficients, repeated over cell sizes and alpha_vir thresholds; also nearest cloud distances for clusters
key_parameters: cell sizes 50 to 200 pixels (110 to 450 pc); alpha_vir thresholds 1 to 3; main bound-cloud map uses alpha_vir < 1.5 and young clusters < 10 Myr

answer_key.quantity: Size-linewidth intercept a0, NGC 7793 (slope fixed at 0.5)

results in values of $X_\text{CO(2-1)}=(0.69-2.56)\times10^{20}$ cm$^{-2}$/(K km s$^{-1}$) for NGC 1313 and $X_\text{CO}$$=(0.64-2.65)\times10^{20}$ cm$^{-2}$/(K km s$^{-1}$) for NGC 7793

score_reason: Score on a 1-5 scale. Project code, calibrators, pipeline/CASA versions, robust values, decomposition parameters and all formulas are given, but the tclean setup, cube definition, noise estimation and bootstrap details are missing and the pipeline version is inconsistent.
rediscovery_reason: ALMA project 2015.1.00782.S is given with archival-style acknowledgement, calibration and decomposition recipes are mostly specified, and main results (intercepts, cluster counts, masses, correlations) are numeric; imaging details must be chosen by the reproducer.
